His desire is met, his longing wholly fulfilled;
the Lord pervades all, ever with him, ever present.
He to whom he belonged has united him with himself.
O Nanak, through devotion he merges in the Naam.
a20.p4: How can he be forgotten, who does not let our toil go to waste?
How can he be forgotten, who recognises what we have done?
How can he be forgotten, who has given us everything?
How can he be forgotten, who is the life of all beings?
How can he be forgotten, who keeps us safe in the fire (of the womb)?
By the Guru's grace only a rare one perceives this.
How can he be forgotten, who draws us out of poison,
and joins again those parted from him for lifetimes?
The perfect Guru has made this essential truth clear.
O Nanak, his servants have meditated on their God.
a20.p5: give up all else and repeat the Lord's Name.
Remember, remember, remember him, and find peace.
Repeat the Naam yourselves and have others repeat it.
Through loving devotion the world-ocean is crossed;
without devotion the body will turn to ashes.
The Naam is the treasure of every blessing and comfort;
even one who is drowning finds rest in it.
Says Nanak, repeat the Naam of the Lord, the treasure of virtues.
a20.p6: Love has welled up in me, the sweetness of love, and longing;
within mind and body this alone is my aim:
to behold the sight of him with my eyes and be at peace.
The mind blossoms as it washes the feet of the Saadhs.
The devotees are dyed in his love, mind and body;
only a rare one gains their company.
Be merciful and give me one thing:
that by the Guru's grace I may repeat the Naam.
O Nanak, he is present in all.
a20.p7: God is forgiving, merciful to the meek.
He loves his devotees and is ever kind.
He is Master of the masterless, Gobind (the Lord of the universe), Gopal (the sustainer of the world);
He is the Primal Being, the cause of all, the Creator,
he is the mainstay of his devotees' lives.
Whoever repeats his Name becomes pure,
fixing the mind's love on him in loving devotion.
We are without virtue, lowly and ignorant.
Nanak is in your refuge, Lord, Supreme Being.
a20.p8: All the heavens, freedom and liberation are gained
by singing the Lord's praises for a single moment.
Many kingdoms, pleasures and honours belong to one
whose mind delights in the telling of the Lord's Name.
Many foods, garments and music are his
whose tongue repeats Har Har every day.
Good are his deeds, glorious and rich is he
in whose heart dwells the perfect Guru's teaching.
God, let me dwell in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy).
O Nanak, there every comfort shines forth.
a21.salok: He himself has qualities and is beyond qualities; he is the Formless One, absorbed in the trance of the void (sunn samadhi).
O Nanak, he himself made all this, and he himself, in turn, meditates on himself.
a21.p1: When none of this visible world could be seen,
where then could sin and merit come from?
When he himself had entered his own trance of the void,
then with whom could anyone practise hatred and strife?
When the world had no colour or mark to be seen,
then tell me, whom could joy and grief take hold of?
When the Supreme Lord was all alone, by himself,
then where was attachment, and who could have doubt?
He himself has set his own play in motion.
O Nanak, there is no other doer.
a21.p2: When God the Master alone existed,
then tell me, who could be counted bound or free?
When there was only the Lord, unreachable and infinite,
then tell me, who could be born into hell or heaven?
When God was beyond qualities, in his own natural poise,
then tell me, where were Shiva and Shakti (spirit and matter)?
When he kept his own light within himself,
then who was without fear, and who feared what?
He himself performs his own wondrous plays.
O Nanak, the Master is unreachable and infinite.
a21.p3: When the Imperishable was seated at ease in his own place,
then tell me, where were birth, death and destruction?
When there was only that perfect Creator God,
then tell me, who could feel the terror of the messenger of Death?
When God, unmanifest and beyond the senses, was the One alone,
then of whom could Chitra and Gupta (the recorders of deeds) ask an account?
When there was only the Master, stainless, beyond the senses and unfathomable,
then who was set free, and who was tied in bonds?
He himself, by himself, is the wonder.
O Nanak, he himself gave rise to his own form.
a21.p4: Where the pure Being, Master of all beings, was alone,
there was no dirt; tell me, what could be washed?
Where there was only the stainless, formless One, free of all desire,
there who had honour, and who had pride?
Where the Lord of the world was present in his own form alone,
there, tell me, whom could deceit and fault cling to?
Where the One whose being is light was merged in his own light,
there who was hungry, and who could be satisfied?
He is the Creator, who does and causes all to be done.
O Nanak, the Creator is beyond all reckoning.
a21.p5: When he had made his glory with himself alone,
then who was mother, father, friend, son or brother?
Where he himself was master of every power,
there where were the Vedas and the Katebs (the Semitic scriptures), and who was there to recognise them?
When he held himself within himself,
then who could weigh good omens and bad?
Where he himself was the high and himself the near,
there who could be called master, and who servant?
We are lost in wonder upon wonder, amazed.
Says Nanak, you alone know your own state.
a21.p6: Where the One who cannot be deceived, pierced or divided was absorbed in himself,
there whom could Maya (the world's illusion and lure) take hold of?
He bowed in homage to himself alone;
the three qualities of Maya had no entry there.
Where there was only the One, the one Lord alone,
there who was free of care, and who could be touched by care?
Where he himself was content within himself,
there who was to speak, and who to listen?
He is vast and endless, higher than the highest.
O Nanak, he alone can reach himself.
a21.p7: When he himself fashioned the visible expanse of the world,
he spread it out within the three qualities.
Then came talk of sin and merit;
one is bound for hell, another longs for heaven.
The snares of household life and the entanglements of Maya,
the burdens of Haumai (ego), attachment, doubt and fear,
pain and pleasure, honour and dishonour:
all these came to be told of in many ways.
He himself stages his own play and watches it.
When he winds up the play, O Nanak, then he alone remains.
a21.p8: Where the devotee of the Unmanifest is, there he himself is.
Where he spreads out the expanse of creation, it is for the glory of his Sants (saints).
He is himself the Master of both sides;
He himself performs his plays, his joyful wonders;
he himself enjoys every pleasure and yet remains untouched.
Whom he pleases, he attaches to his Name;
whom he pleases, he makes play the game of the world.
He is beyond count, fathomless, numberless and beyond weighing.
As you make him speak, so your servant Nanak speaks.
a22.salok: Master of every being and creature, you yourself are present and at work in all.
O Nanak, the One alone is spread out everywhere; what other can be seen?
a22.p1: He himself speaks, and he himself listens.
He himself is One, and he himself has spread out as all.
When it pleases him, he brings forth the creation;
by his own will he draws it back into himself.
you have strung the whole world on your own thread.
The one to whom God himself gives understanding,
that servant receives the true Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered).
He looks on all alike and knows the essence of reality.
O Nanak, he is the conqueror of the whole world.
a22.p2: He holds all beings and creatures in his hands;
merciful to the meek, he is the Master of the masterless.
One whom he protects, no one can kill;
that one is dead whom he puts out of his mind.
Forsaking him, where else can one go?
Above every head is the one stainless King.
He in whose hand lie all the ways of every being,
know him to be with you, within and without.
He is the treasure of virtues, endless and infinite.
His servant Nanak is ever a sacrifice to him.
a22.p3: The merciful one fills every place to the full,
and he shows kindness to all.
He alone knows what he does;
the knower of hearts is present throughout.
He cherishes his beings in many ways;
whatever he has created meditates on him.
Whom he pleases, he unites with himself;
they worship him, singing the Lord's praises.
With faith in their hearts they have believed in him.
O Nanak, they have known the one Creator.
a22.p4: The Lord's servant is attached to the Name of the one Lord,
and his hope does not go in vain.
To the servant, service comes naturally;
understanding the Hukam (God's will and command), he attains the supreme state.
There is no thought higher than this
for one in whose mind the Formless Lord dwells.
Breaking their bonds, they have become free of enmity;
night and day they worship the Guru's feet.
They are happy in this world and at ease in the world hereafter.
O Nanak, the Lord God himself has united them with himself.
a22.p5: Join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and rejoice;
sing the praises of God, the supreme bliss.
Reflect on the Lord's Name, the essence of all,
and redeem this body so hard to obtain.
Sing the Lord's praises, words of nectar;
this is the way for the soul to cross over.
At all hours see God near you;
ignorance will end and darkness be destroyed.
Hear the teaching and enshrine it in your heart.
Says Nanak, you will receive the fruit your heart desires.
a22.p6: Set right both this life and the life hereafter:
keep the Lord's Name enshrined deep in your heart.
The teaching of the perfect Guru is perfect;
one in whose mind it dwells has recognised the Truth.
With mind and body repeat the Naam, attuned to him in love;
pain, suffering and fear will leave the mind.
Trader, deal in the true trade,
and your cargo will come safely through to the Lord's court.
Within your mind keep the One alone as your support.
Says Nanak, you will not come and go again.
a22.p7: Where can anyone go far from him?
One is saved by meditating on the Protector.
When one repeats the Name of the Fearless One, all fear is erased;
by God's grace a mortal is set free.
One whom God protects has no pain;
repeating the Naam, the mind finds peace.
Anxiety goes and pride is erased;
no one can equal that servant.
The valiant Guru stands over his head.
O Nanak, his tasks are all fulfilled.
a22.p8: Perfect is the wisdom of him whose glance is nectar;
at the sight of him the world is saved.
fruitful is the sight of the Lord, and beautiful his form.
Blessed is his service, and his servant is accepted;
he is the knower of hearts, the Supreme Being.
One in whose mind he dwells is filled with joy;
death does not come near him.
They have become immortal and attained the immortal state,
O Nanak, who meditated on the Lord in the Saadh Sangat.
a23.salok: The Guru has given the salve of divine knowledge for the eyes, and ignorance and its darkness are gone.
When by the Lord's grace one meets the Sant (saint), O Nanak, the mind is lit up.
a23.p1: In the company of the Sants I have seen God within;
God's Name tastes sweet to me.
All things are within the heart of the One,
though they appear in many colours and kinds.
God's Name is the nectar, the nine treasures;
its resting place is within the body.
There is the trance of the void, and there the unstruck melody sounds, the divine music that no instrument makes;
its wonder and amazement cannot be told.
He alone has seen it to whom God himself has shown it.
O Nanak, that servant gains understanding.
a23.p2: The Infinite One is within, and he is without;
In the earth, the sky and the regions below,
in all the worlds, he is the perfect sustainer.
In forest, grass and mountain is the Supreme Lord;
as his command is, so is every deed.
He is in air, water and fire;
he fills the four corners and the ten directions.
There is no place apart from him.
By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, find peace.
a23.p3: See him in Vedas, Puranas and Simritis;
the One is in moon, sun and stars.
Everyone speaks the speech of God;
he himself is steady and never wavers.
With all his powers he plays his play;
he cannot be bought at any price, and his virtues are priceless.
He whose light is in every light,
that Master upholds all, woven through like warp and weft.
By the Guru's grace doubt comes to an end.
O Nanak, in them this faith becomes firm.
a23.p4: To the Sants all they behold is God;
in the hearts of the Sants is all righteousness.
The Sants hear words of good;
they are merged in the Lord who pervades all.
Such is the conduct of one who has known him:
all that the Saadh (holy one) says is true.
Whatever happens, he accepts it gladly;
he knows God as the one who does and causes all to be done.
For him God dwells within, and outside too it is he alone.
O Nanak, at the sight of him all are enchanted.
a23.p5: He is true himself, and true is everything he has made;
from that God came the whole creation.
When it pleases him, he spreads out the creation;
when it pleases him, he is Ekankar (the One Creator) alone again.
His many powers cannot be grasped;
whom he pleases, he unites with himself.
Who can be called near, and who far?
He himself is all, filling everything.
One whom he himself makes aware of his presence within,
O Nanak, to that servant he himself gives understanding.
a23.p6: He himself is at work in all beings;
through all eyes he himself is the one who sees.
he himself hears his own praise.
The One has made coming and going a play;
he has made Maya (the world's illusion and lure) obey his command.
whatever there is to say, he says it himself.
By his command one comes, by his command one goes.
O Nanak, when it pleases him, he takes them back into himself.
a23.p7: Whatever comes from him is not bad;
tell me, apart from him, has anyone done anything?
He himself is good, and his works are excellent beyond measure;
he alone knows his own heart.
He himself is the Truth, and all he upholds is true;
woven through and through, he is absorbed in his own creation.
No one can tell his state or his extent;
only if there were another like him could that one understand.
All that he does is to be accepted.
By the Guru's grace, says Nanak, know this.
a23.p8: One who knows this has peace for ever;
that God himself unites him with himself.
He is wealthy, of noble family and honoured;
liberated while living is the one in whose heart the Lord dwells.
Blessed, blessed, blessed is that servant's coming,
by whose grace the whole world is carried across.
This is the purpose of such a servant's coming:
that in his company the Name comes to mind.
He himself is free, and he sets the world free.
O Nanak, salutations for ever to that servant.
a24.salok: The perfect God has been worshipped, whose Name too is perfect.
Says Nanak, the Perfect One has been found; sing the praises of the Perfect One.
a24.p1: Listen to the perfect Guru's teaching,
and behold the Supreme Lord near you.
Remember Gobind (the Lord of the universe) with every breath;
the worry in your mind will lift.
Let go of the waves of fleeting hope;
ask, my mind, for the dust of the feet of the Sants (saints).
Set aside self-conceit and make your prayer;
cross the ocean of fire in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy).
Fill your storehouses with the Lord's wealth.
O Nanak, salutations to the perfect Guru.
a24.p2: For well-being, happiness, poise and bliss,
worship the Lord of supreme bliss in the Saadh Sangat.
Ward off hell and save your soul;
drink the nectar of Gobind's praises.
In your heart dwell on the one all-pervading Lord,
whose form is one and whose colours are many.
He is Gopal (the sustainer of the world), Damodar (a name of the Lord), merciful to the meek,
Remember, remember the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered), again and again.
O Nanak, this alone sustains the soul.
a24.p3: The words of the Saadh (holy one) are verses of the highest praise;
they are priceless rubies and gems.
Hearing them and living by them, one is saved;
such a one crosses over and carries others across.
Fruitful is the life, and fruitful the company,
of one whose mind is dyed in the Lord's love.
For him the unstruck Word of victory resounds;
hearing it again and again he rejoices, and God thunders forth within him.
Gopal shines forth on the foreheads of the great souls.
O Nanak, in their company people are saved.
a24.p4: Hearing that he is able to give refuge, we have come to his refuge;
in his grace God has united us with himself.
Enmity has vanished, and we have become the dust of all;
in the Saadh Sangat we receive the Naam, which is nectar.
The divine Guru is well pleased,
and his servant's service is fulfilled.
We are kept free of household entanglements and vice,
hearing the Lord's Name and repeating it with the tongue.
In his kindness God has shown mercy.
Says Nanak, our cargo has come safely through.
a24.p5: with a mind alert and fixed on him alone.
The Sukhmani, the jewel of peace, is poise, Gobind's praises and the Naam;
one in whose mind it dwells becomes a treasure-house.
he becomes the foremost of men, renowned in all the world.
He reaches the highest place of all,
and he comes and goes no more.
that servant alone departs having earned the wealth of the Lord:
O Nanak, the one to whom it is granted.
a24.p6: Well-being, peace, prosperity and the nine treasures;
wisdom, knowledge and every spiritual power;
learning, austerity, yoga and meditation on God;
the highest knowledge and the most purifying bath;
the four great blessings and the blossoming of the heart-lotus;
living amid all and yet detached from all;
beauty, insight and knowledge of the essence of reality;
looking on all alike and seeing the One alone:
these fruits come to that servant who speaks the Naam with his mouth,
and with his mind hears the word of the Naam from Guru Nanak.
a24.p7: Whoever repeats this treasure in the mind,
he is liberated, in every age.
This Bani, the Guru's word, holds the praises of Gobind and the melody of the Naam,
of which the Simritis, Shastras and Vedas speak.
The Lord's Name alone is the essence of all creeds;
it rests in the minds of Gobind's devotees.
In the Saadh Sangat millions of sins are erased;
the Sant's grace frees one from the messenger of Death.
Those on whose foreheads God has written his grace,
O Nanak, they come to the refuge of the Saadh.
a24.p8: One in whose mind it dwells, who hears it lovingly:
into that servant's mind the Lord God comes.
His pain of birth and death is taken away;
this body, so hard to obtain, is redeemed at once.
Spotless is his glory, and his speech is nectar;
the one Name fills his mind.
Pain, sickness, fear and doubt are gone;
he is called a Saadh, and his deeds are spotless.
It is for these virtues, O Nanak, that its name is Sukhmani, the jewel of peace.
